notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: M5 is true provider-managed rotation, not merely creating a new local SecretVersion. Rotation must be modeled as create -> distribute -> verify -> revoke, with provider-specific capability declarations and rollback/failure handling.

notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: Roadmap renumbered after splitting secure core from runtime secrets; now M6.

problem: Distribution and expiry metadata do not rotate a credential at its source. Real rotation requires provider-specific creation, propagation, verification and revocation without causing outages.
rollback: Keep the old provider credential valid until propagation and verification of the new credential succeeds.
If verification fails, restore bindings to the previous known-good SecretVersion and do not revoke the old provider credential.
Allow provider rotation plugins to degrade to manual-action-required when safe rollback cannot be guaranteed.
scope: Extend target/integration plugin capabilities to declare provider-managed credential creation, validation and revocation operations.
Model rotation as an explicit state machine rather than a single update call.
Create a new credential at a supported provider, store it as a new SecretVersion and propagate it through existing SyncBindings.
Verify deployment/target acceptance using provider-appropriate checks before revoking the previous credential.
Revoke the old provider credential only after successful propagation and verification, unless a human explicitly overrides policy.
Record every rotation transition and actor in audit.
Implement provider-managed rotation for only one or a very small number of first-party providers initially; broad provider coverage is not part of M5.
title: Milestone 6: provider-managed credential rotation
validation: A supported credential can complete create -> distribute -> verify -> revoke while maintaining a visible rotation state throughout the operation.
The old credential is not revoked if distribution or verification fails.
A failed rotation exposes a clear recovery action and preserves a known-good credential path.
Audit can reconstruct who initiated/approved rotation, each transition, affected targets and final outcome without containing secret plaintext.
Providers that do not support safe automated rotation are reported as unsupported or manual rather than approximated with unsafe behavior.
value: Move from secret distribution to full credential lifecycle automation while minimizing outage and stale-credential risk.
